packageRules.description: The workflows' go-version inputs (depName `go`) and the two .tool-versions pins (depNames `golang` and `golangci-lint`) all track the same toolchain; bump them in one PR. golangci-lint especially cannot lag: it type-checks through a vendored x/tools that only reads export data from Go releases it already knows about.

A pin fixes a floating tag to the version already in use, so there is no newer release to age. Renovate synthesizes pin updates with no releaseTimestamp, and the default minimumReleaseAgeBehaviour of timestamp-required holds those pending forever.

Go indirect dependencies are disabled by default, which also silently swallows their security advisories: x/crypto sat on 33 CVEs with skipReason `disabled` and no update. Enable them so advisories can reach them, but park the routine ones behind a dashboard checkbox — there are ~40 and none earns a PR on its own. The vulnerabilityAlerts config force-sets dependencyDashboardApproval to false, so an indirect dep with a CVE still gets an immediate PR, and skips both minimumReleaseAge and the concurrency limits.

The AWS SDK ships ~35 separately versioned modules that release in lockstep. Ungrouped, they would never drain at prConcurrentLimit 1. This rule must stay below the indirect rule above: later rules win, and generateBranchConfig derives a branch's dependencyDashboardApproval with `.some()` over its upgrades, so one gated upgrade gates the whole branch. This group is the one place where direct and indirect gomod deps share a branch, so without the override here its 15 indirect modules would park the 14 direct ones behind a checkbox. MVS drags them forward with their direct siblings anyway.
